results.summary: This project is titled test001 and is described only as a test Tiny Tapeout design. The documentation consists of placeholder text asking how the project works and how to test it, with no actual explanation. The pin names map the eight outputs to the segments and dot of a 7-segment display, but nothing states what is driven onto them. There is not enough information to determine the design's function or how it should be used.

This design implements four basic logic gates on a single tile: an AND of inputs 0 and 1, a NAND of inputs 2 and 3, an OR of inputs 4 and 5, and an XOR of inputs 6 and 7, with the results on outputs 0 through 3. It was created as an example for a Supercon workshop, presumably to teach the Tiny Tapeout design flow. The design is built using the Wokwi online simulator. It is intended for educational purposes, demonstrating simple combinational logic.

This design is an 8-bit binary counter built from eight chained D flip-flops that increment on the clock input and present the count on the eight outputs. It is created as part of a workshop and uses the Wokwi simulator. The design is intended for educational purposes, demonstrating sequential logic. The pin names map the outputs to 7-segment display segments, but no function is described.
